ei.title: Why an Integrated Approach to Ageing and Gut Health Is Necessary

fullPassage: As well as the ageing process itself, getting old is associated with other factors which drive changes in our microbiome. Our gut flora is heavily influenced by our diet, since the microbes effectively share what we eat. Older people's diets often change significantly, sometimes for trivial-sounding reasons, like consuming less fruit because it gets harder to eat as we lose our teeth. This is a beautifully simple example of why it's so important to treat the whole ageing process, and not do medicine in silos ― better dentistry doesn't just mean less toothache, but it also has impacts on diet which have wider knock-on effects of their own. The elderly are also prescribed more antibiotics, which can damage the microbiome at the same time as treating the bacteria making them ill. There's also a significant environmental component to your microbial family, and older people living in care often have a different spectrum of species from those still living at home.

questions.passage: As well as the ageing process itself, getting old is associated with other factors which drive changes in our microbiome. Our gut flora is heavily (A)[influenced / ignored] by our diet, since the microbes effectively share what we eat. Older people's diets often change significantly, sometimes for trivial-sounding reasons, like consuming less fruit because it gets harder to eat as we lose our teeth. This is a beautifully simple example of why it's so important to treat the whole ageing process, and not do medicine in silos ― better dentistry doesn't just mean less toothache, but it also has impacts on diet which have wider knock-on effects of their own. The elderly are also prescribed more antibiotics, which can (B)[damage / strengthen] the microbiome at the same time as treating the bacteria making them ill. There's also a significant (C)[environmental / fictional] component to your microbial family, and older people living in care often have a different spectrum of species from those still living at home.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ① influenced - damage - environmental: 장내 세균이 식단에 '영향을 받고', 항생제가 미생물군을 '손상시키며', 미생물 가족에 '환경적' 요인이 있다는 원문.
❌ ② ignored - damage - environmental: '무시되는'은 heavily influenced와 반대.
❌ ③ influenced - strengthen - environmental: '강화하다'는 damage(손상)의 반대.
❌ ④ influenced - damage - fictional: '허구의'는 환경적 요인과 맞지 않음.
det.tip: influenced(영향을 받는) ↔ ignored(무시되는). damage(손상시키다) ↔ strengthen(강화하다).

questions.passage: As well as the ageing process itself, getting old is (A)[associated / unrelated] with other factors which drive changes in our microbiome. Our gut flora is heavily influenced by our diet, since the microbes effectively share what we eat. Older people's diets often change (B)[significantly / slightly], sometimes for trivial-sounding reasons, like consuming less fruit because it gets harder to eat as we lose our teeth. This is a beautifully simple example of why it's so important to treat the whole ageing process, and not do medicine in silos ― better dentistry doesn't just mean less toothache, but it also has impacts on diet which have wider knock-on effects of their own. The elderly are also (C)[prescribed / forbidden] more antibiotics, which can damage the microbiome at the same time as treating the bacteria making them ill. There's also a significant environmental component to your microbial family, and older people living in care often have a different spectrum of species from those still living at home.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ② associated - significantly - prescribed: 노화가 다른 요인들과 '관련되고', 식단이 '상당히' 변하며, 노인에게 항생제가 더 많이 '처방된다'는 원문.
❌ ① unrelated - significantly - prescribed: '관련 없는'은 associated와 반대.
❌ ③ associated - slightly - prescribed: '약간'은 significantly와 반대.
❌ ④ associated - significantly - forbidden: '금지되는'은 prescribed와 반대.
det.tip: associated with(~와 관련된) ↔ unrelated to. significantly(상당히) ↔ slightly(약간). prescribed(처방된) ↔ forbidden(금지된).

The elderly are also prescribed more antibiotics, which can damage the microbiome at the same time as treating the bacteria making them ill. questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ③ trivial - whole - knock-on: 이유가 '사소하게' 들리지만, 노화 과정 '전체'를 치료해야 하며, 식단 변화가 더 넓은 '연쇄적' 효과를 갖는다는 원문.
❌ ① critical - whole - knock-on: '중대한'은 trivial-sounding과 반대.
❌ ② trivial - partial - knock-on: '부분적'은 whole(전체)과 반대.
❌ ④ trivial - whole - isolated: '고립된'은 연쇄적 효과와 반대.
det.tip: trivial(사소한) ↔ critical(중대한). whole(전체) ↔ partial(부분적). knock-on(연쇄적) ↔ isolated(고립된).

questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중에서 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.analysis:

questions.stem: 밑줄 친 <u>prescribed</u>와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.tip: prescribe(처방하다) → prescribed(처방된). 의사가 약을 처방하다.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ④ an integrated, whole-body approach: 분리 진료(silos) 반대, 전체 노화 과정(the whole ageing process) 치료 강조.
❌ ① only dental treatment: 치과 치료만으로는 불충분 — 본문은 통합 접근 강조.
❌ ② fewer antibiotics for everyone: 항생제 감소 권고는 본문의 핵심이 아님.
❌ ③ a completely new diet plan: 완전히 새로운 식단 계획은 본문에 없음.
det.tip: not do medicine in silos = 분리 진료 금지. treat the whole = 통합적 접근.

✅ ③ 노인에게 항생제가 더 많이 처방된다: 'The elderly are also prescribed more antibiotics' — 일치.
❌ ④ 요양원의 노인과 자택 거주 노인의 미생물 종 구성은 같다: 본문은 'different spectrum' — 다르다고 함.

✅ ④ 더 나은 치과 진료의 효과는 치통 감소에 국한된다: 본문은 'doesn't just mean less toothache, but it also has impacts on diet which have wider knock-on effects' — 치통 감소에 국한되지 않음.
❌ ③ 노인의 미생물 가족에 환경적 요인이 있다: 'a significant environmental component' — 일치.
det.tip: doesn't just mean X, but also Y = X에만 국한되지 않고 Y도.

questions.passage: As well as the ageing process itself, getting old is associated with other factors which drive changes in our microbiome. Our gut __________ is heavily influenced by our diet, since the microbes effectively share what we eat. Older people's diets often change significantly, sometimes for trivial-sounding reasons, like consuming less fruit because it gets harder to eat as we lose our teeth. This is a beautifully simple example of why it's so important to treat the whole ageing process, and not do medicine in silos ― better dentistry doesn't just mean less toothache, but it also has impacts on diet which have wider knock-on effects of their own. The elderly are also prescribed more antibiotics, which can damage the microbiome at the same time as treating the bacteria making them ill. There's also a significant environmental component to your microbial family, and older people living in care often have a different spectrum of species from those still living at home.

det.tip: flora(식물군, 세균군). gut flora = 장내 세균군 = microbiome.
